newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire Central Bank closes as employees strike.
newsitem.headline: Zaire Central Bank closes as employees strike.

text.p: Around 2,000 employees of Zaire's Central Bank went on strike on Friday, demanding an end-of-year bonus and restoration of transport allowances.

Employees picketed the vast building in the capital's Gombe district, effectively forcing the bank's closure for the day. Troops guarded the building behind a large iron fence, as bank staff shouted their demands.

"It is us who print the nation's money, but at the end of the month we don't see any of it, they treat us like pigs," said a 41-year-old printer who asked to remain anonymous. He said his pay, equivalent to $50 a month, often went unpayed.
The staff are demanding an end-of-year bonus of one month's salary and restoration of transport supplements they say were scrapped two years ago.
Bank of Zaire governor Patrice Djamboleka and other officials held meetings on Friday to try to solve the problem.

"The bank hierarchy has in principle agreed to pay the end-of-year bonus. Only we have a problem of liquidity. We had agreed to give them the bonus at a later stage but the staff are impatient," a Bank official said.

Traditionally the Bank's 3,000-plus staff are among Zaire's best-paid civil servants but working conditions have deteriorated and salaries have effectively fallen since the beginning of Zaire's democratic transition in 1990.

In the past six years, prolonged periods of galloping inflation have rendered public worker salaries, payed in the local zaire currency, virtually worthless. In 1993, annual inflation hit 8,000 percent.
Other civil servants earn as little as $1 a month.
